// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a648db354820ea4d02940cb1702b35974513b7aae83f6dffaacaac4ba31f9295", "584a9448dda46bd590d7a2f86228100d2ae6e0d6d990c1a4459ed5ee28e07ae8", "66a3836b9a17771bce2161f6b73cbc2494a91e49d6aa30d2d53711e8d10de60d", "4fcfa88fffacbce30bbe2136753c9ab5a4c092940d2406fd9d44d5118e745b9d", "a75eab31d7ff06b6864960ad7e633be3f9730ff3d3873e4539c8f425fc632dad", "40b41979b317406f8abc601677a3b93aaf6ef8ab8ac188b8f383735e388f13b5", "8c9b6542f73c5c7fe455b52f5101314407da4f65ff48e7ebf6896605e607c8d0", "3119cf37b8267db8a2dcd11d9a83d5237d7ef1e42388e7c9afa2831b91da8a2d", "314f4b59535d1b783e1c20c2be00f9e30f8ed27b2e21fad06a73b47ea43279ef", "2d2a251a88632f010fd9671789746908eeccaa5bc5c0a5d25e4649efe4f5b15d", "e0a6a71c605d9a4076147e9537f82f79f1e1eccadc874595160aa4637ff4088c", "de82998ad5fcd63deae030803388e0fb4290d6223fda82368fd25b99b823f0d2", "9d0a55c545c4147956db2c2667c4ed931a2875309147548b1dfdd216228f5f73"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hypotheses, telemetry, and human judgment: Inside Cisco Talos Threat Hunting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest dropping script.ps1 to user AppData (KongTuke stage-2)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path · [LLM] Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path Command & Control High
Hunts the specific KongTuke (TAG-124 / 404 TDS) command-and-control infrastructure named in the Talos case study: outbound HTTP to 144.31.221.82 on TCP/6060 with a URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint. Single-IOC alerting because all three values are article-named. Rationale: Single high-confidence IOC bundle straight from the Talos case-study paragraph: IP 144.31.221.82, TCP/6060, URL path /capcha9856. The /capcha* fingerprint is corroborated by Recorded Future (TAG-124), Red Canary KongTuke profile, and malware-traffic-analysis.net Jan 2026 KongTuke ClickFix capture. Cross-checked via WebSearch — KongTuke is a real, active TDS. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base • https://www.malware-traffic-analysis.net/2026/01/08/index.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002

   or RequestURL has "/capcha9856"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort,
          RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: KongTuke TDS C2 to 144.31.221.82 / capcha URL Path
id: 7e3b1f4e-1f0e-4a2e-9b8d-6b1f4e3c2a01
description: Detects outbound network traffic to KongTuke TDS C2 infrastructure (144.31.221.82:6060) or any URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint reported by Cisco Talos.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
  - https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp: '144.31.221.82'
  selection_port_path:
    DestinationPort: 6060
    DestinationHostname|contains: '/capcha'
  selection_path:
    Url|contains: '/capcha9856'
  condition: selection_ip or selection_port_path or selection_path
falsepositives:
  - None expected; this IP/port/path combination has no known legitimate use.
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 OR source:cisco-firepower OR source:cisco_secure_firewall) AND (@DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 OR (@DestinationPort:6060 AND @DestinationHostname:*\/capcha*) OR @network.destination.ip:144.31.221.82 OR @url:*\/capcha9856*)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82" OR RemotePort=6060)
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/capcha/i}, field=aid, include=[DomainName], mode=left)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])

[LLM] PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest dropping script.ps1 to user AppData (KongTuke stage-2) Installation Medium
Hunts the KongTuke stage-2 download pattern from the Talos case study: a powershell.exe process whose command line invokes Invoke-WebRequest (or iwr) and writes a file named script.ps1 into the user's ApplicationData / AppData directory. Pairs the URL-fetch verb, the article-named filename, and the article-named drop location in one event. Rationale: The combination of three article-named tokens in one PowerShell command line — Invoke-WebRequest verb, exact filename script.ps1, and AppData/ApplicationData drop path — collapses to one cmdline-substring detection that's high specificity. Sourced directly from the Talos KongTuke walk-through (cmd.exe → powershell.exe -EncodedCommand → IWR → script.ps1 → ApplicationData). Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1105 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest", "iwr ", "Net.WebClient", "DownloadFile", "DownloadString")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "script.ps1"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("AppData", "ApplicationData", "\\Roaming\\", "\\Local\\")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest", "iwr ", "Net.WebClient", "DownloadFile", "DownloadString")
| where CommandLine has "script.ps1"
| where CommandLine has_any ("AppData", "ApplicationData", "\\Roaming\\", "\\Local\\")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

tags:

  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_fetch:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'iwr '
      - 'Net.WebClient'
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'DownloadString'
  selection_file:
    CommandLine|contains: 'script.ps1'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'AppData'
      - 'ApplicationData'
      - '\Roaming\'
      - '\Local\'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate internal scripts that happen to fetch a file named script.ps1 into AppData (rare; review user context)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe)) AND (@CommandLine:(*Invoke-WebRequest* OR *iwr\ * OR *Net.WebClient* OR *DownloadFile* OR *DownloadString*)) AND @CommandLine:*script.ps1* AND (@CommandLine:(*AppData* OR *ApplicationData* OR *\\Roaming\\* OR *\\Local\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(Invoke-WebRequest|iwr |Net\.WebClient|DownloadFile|DownloadString)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("script\.ps1", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(AppData|ApplicationData|\\\\Roaming\\\\|\\\\Local\\\\)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Invoke-WebRequest*" OR Processes.process="*iwr *" OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*") Processes.process="*script.ps1*" (Processes.process="*AppData*" OR Processes.process="*ApplicationData*" OR Processes.process="*\\Roaming\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\Local\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Invoke-WebRequest*" OR Processes.process="*iwr *" OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*") Processes.process="*script.ps1*" (Processes.process="*AppData*" OR Processes.process="*ApplicationData*" OR Processes.process="*\\Roaming\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\Local\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window Command & Control High
Reproduces the Talos multi-source-correlation insight: the same endpoint reaching 144.31.221.82 from two distinct binaries (powershell.exe via Invoke-WebRequest and curl.exe directly) is the disambiguating signal that turned a single firewall hit into a confirmed intrusion. Single-binary callouts to the IP are already caught by UC1; this UC fires on the host-level fan-out only. Rationale: Directly encodes the Talos case-study insight: 'a separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' Two distinct LOLBin/native binaries calling the same KongTuke IP from one host is high-fidelity even without the URL-path filter — it's the multi-process fan-out that confirms intrusion vs single-shot scanning. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "144.31.221.82" or (RemotePort == 6060 and RemoteUrl has "/capcha")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "curl.exe")
| summarize ProcessSet = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            FirstConnection = min(Timestamp),
            LastConnection = max(Timestamp),
            ConnectionCount = count(),
            CmdLines = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 8)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where array_length(ProcessSet) >= 2
| where (ProcessSet has "curl.exe") and (ProcessSet has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"))
| order by FirstConnection desc
let WindowHours = 1h;
let FirewallHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DestinationIP == "144.31.221.82" or (DestinationPort == 6060 and RequestURL has "/capcha")
    | project FirewallTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL;
let ProcessHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("144.31.221.82", "capcha", "script.ps1")
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | project ProcessTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, SubjectUserName;
FirewallHits
| join kind=inner (
    ProcessHits
    | summarize Procs=make_set(NewProcessName), AnyCmd=make_set(CommandLine, 8) by Computer
    | where array_length(Procs) >= 2
) on $left.SourceIP == $right.Computer
| order by FirewallTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\Curl.exe OR *\\CURL.EXE)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82"
| ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|curl)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[collect([ContextImageFileName]), count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
| length(ContextImageFileName) >= 2
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(Processes.process_name) as distinct_procs values(Processes.process_name) as procs values(Processes.process) as cmdlines min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe") (Processes.process="*144.31.221.82*" OR Processes.process="*capcha*") by Processes.dest Processes.user host
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where distinct_procs >= 2
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Processes.process_name) as distinct_procs values(Processes.process_name) as procs values(Processes.process) as cmdlines min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe") (Processes.process="*144.31.221.82*" OR Processes.process="*capcha*") by Processes.dest Processes.user host
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where distinct_procs >= 2

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

| order by Timestamp desc

FlutterShell Backdoor Spreads to macOS via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads

The Hacker News
2026-06-04 12 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have shed light on a macOS malvertising campaign codenamed Operation FlutterBridge that spreads a new backdoor called FlutterShell. According to Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, the campaign is said to be the next stage of a previously reported activity cluster dubbed JSCoreRunner (aka FileRipple) in late August 2025. The cybercrime group behind the two attack chains is

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Chrome Preferences tamper on macOS by non-Chrome process (FlutterShell browser hijack) · [LLM] Known FlutterShell SHA256 binary execution on macOS · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] macOS host beaconing to FlutterShell C2 / ad-intermediary domains · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] FlutterShell WebView bridge spawns shell on macOS (arbitrary command execution capability) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Chrome Preferences tamper on macOS by non-Chrome process (FlutterShell browser hijack) Installation High
FlutterShell rewrites Google Chrome configuration files on macOS to force traffic through an attacker-controlled ad-intermediary site. This hunts writes to Chrome's Preferences/Local State by any process other than Chrome itself, which is the article-specific browser-hijack tell. Rationale: Anchors on the article's most specific operational behaviour: "modifies Google Chrome configuration files to hijack the browser, forcing all traffic through an attacker-controlled, ad-filled intermediary site." Filtering for non-Chrome writers eliminates almost all baseline Chrome self-writes. Cross-checked against Unit 42 / Palo Alto Networks blog coverage of JSCoreRunner/FileRipple. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
ATT&CKT1176 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/"
| where FileName in~ ("Preferences","Secure Preferences","Local State")
| where ActionType in ("FileModified","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("Google Chrome","Google Chrome Helper","chrome","Keystone"))
| where not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Preferences","Secure Preferences","Local State")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("Google Chrome","chrome","Keystone"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
title: Non-Chrome Process Modifies Chrome Preferences on macOS
id: 9e2a3f51-5b8a-4f6d-9c2a-7d4b1c0e5a11
description: Detects modification of Google Chrome Preferences / Local State files on macOS by any process other than Chrome itself, indicative of FlutterShell-style browser-hijack adware redirecting traffic through an attacker-controlled intermediary.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fluttershell-backdoor-spreads-to-macos.html
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/
author: SOC Detection Eng
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1176
  - attack.t1539
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: macos
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Preferences'
      - '/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Secure Preferences'
      - '/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Local State'
  filter_chrome:
    Image|contains:
      - '/Google Chrome.app/'
      - '/Keystone.app/'
  condition: selection and not filter_chrome
level: high

[LLM] macOS host beaconing to FlutterShell C2 / ad-intermediary domains Command & Control High
Hunts DNS resolution or network connections from macOS endpoints to the article's named FlutterShell infrastructure (ads-parkpro/adsparkpro/softwe.art front-company domains plus the four C2 cover domains). High-fidelity given the IOCs come straight from Unit 42's IOC list and are unlikely to appear in any legitimate macOS workload. Rationale: Direct match on Unit 42's named infrastructure for Operation FlutterBridge. Domains correspond to article-stated front companies (AdsParkPro LTD, SOFT WE ART LIMITED) and C2 cover. Domains have no legitimate use in any enterprise; one hit warrants an alert. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://urlhaus.abuse.ch/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.001

let net = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (c2_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let dns = DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","InboundConnectionAccepted")
| extend QName = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).QueryName)
| where QName has_any (c2_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, QName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
union net, dns
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2_domains = dynamic(["atsheisdomestic.org","etoftheappyrince.org","healightejustb.org","sinterfumesco.com","ads-parkpro.com","adsparkpro.top","adsparkpro.net","softwe.art"]);

[LLM] Known FlutterShell SHA256 binary execution on macOS Installation High
Direct hash-match alert on the eight FlutterShell SHA256s published by Unit 42 for the PodcastsLounge / PDF-Brain / PDF-Ninja variants. Defender XDR + Sentinel + Falcon all surface SHA256 on process telemetry — minimum-friction high-fidelity tripwire for in-the-wild samples. Rationale: Unit 42 IOC SHA256s are tier-1 confidence and shared across three FlutterShell variants. Notarized signing means file-reputation alone won't catch these; hash-match is the cleanest tripwire. Cross-referenced against Unit 42 IOC bundle. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.virustotal.com/

[LLM] FlutterShell WebView bridge spawns shell on macOS (arbitrary command execution capability) Actions on Objectives Medium
FlutterShell uses a JavaScript-to-native bridge inside a WebView to invoke shell commands on demand from attacker-controlled JavaScript. Hunts macOS Flutter-style apps (signed with the article's known shell-company developers, or matching the named variant binary names) spawning /bin/sh, /bin/bash, /usr/bin/zsh, /usr/bin/osascript — the smoking-gun behaviour of the JS-bridge backdoor. Rationale: Anchors on the article's three named variant binaries (PodcastsLounge, PDF-Brain, PDF-Ninja) AND the WebView-JS-bridge architecture that necessitates spawning a shell to execute attacker-supplied commands. A legitimate PDF reader or podcast app has no reason to fork /bin/sh. The signer-name pivot (AdsParkPro / Advantage Web Marketing / SOFT WE ART / PACIFIC TRADE SOLUTIONS) catches future variants that change the binary name. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PodcastsLounge","PDF-Brain","PDF-Ninja")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/PodcastsLounge.app/","/PDF-Brain.app/","/PDF-Ninja.app/")
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has_any ("AdsParkPro","Advantage Web Marketing","SOFT WE ART","PACIFIC TRADE SOLUTIONS")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","zsh","dash","osascript","curl","python","python3","env")
| extend HasShellArgs = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","-c\"","-e ","do shell script","printenv","env")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, HasShellArgs
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("PodcastsLounge","PDF-Brain","PDF-Ninja")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("/PodcastsLounge.app/","/PDF-Brain.app/","/PDF-Ninja.app/")
   or ActingProcessFileCompany has_any ("AdsParkPro","Advantage Web Marketing","SOFT WE ART","PACIFIC TRADE SOLUTIONS")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/bin/zsh","/bin/dash","/usr/bin/osascript","/usr/bin/curl","/usr/bin/python","/usr/bin/python3","/usr/bin/env")
| extend HasShellArgs = TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","do shell script","printenv","env")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessFileCompany, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, HasShellArgs, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union

        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

        | where SHA256 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or SHA1 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or MD5 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745")

        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools Rank High on Google to Deliver Malware via TDS

The Hacker News
2026-06-04 15 use cases 9 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged a large-scale operation that impersonates open-source and freeware projects to funnel unsuspecting users through a Traffic Distribution System (TDS) and deliver malware families like Remus Stealer, AnimateClipper, and the SessionGate framework. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Outbound contact to fake open-source tool / TDS / CloudFront staging domains · [LLM] Browser-spawned executable/installer drop within 5 min of TDS site contact · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] AnimateClipper ClickFix paste-to-run via explorer.exe spawning mshta/powershell/cmd · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SessionGate final-stage rundll32 spawning cmd.exe to fetch and silently execute next-stage payload · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Remus/Lumma Stealer browser-credential and crypto-wallet directory enumeration · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Outbound contact to fake open-source tool / TDS / CloudFront staging domains Delivery High
Detects host or browser contact (DNS or HTTP) with the eight typosquatted Ghidra/dnSpy/SpiderFoot/grpcurl lookalike sites and the CloudFront-hosted staging layer + downstream TDS endpoints used to deliver SessionGate, Remus Stealer and AnimateClipper. Rationale: Eight domains pulled verbatim from the Check Point breakdown / pre-extracted IOC block (grpcurl.com, ghidralite.com, two CloudFront staging hosts, plus four TDS endpoints). All are confirmed by Check Point and the November 2025 Fullstory write-up referenced in the article body — high-fidelity atomic IOCs. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/ • https://www.fullstory.com/blog/

[LLM] Browser-spawned executable/installer drop within 5 min of TDS site contact Delivery High
Time-window correlation between a browser visit to a TDS / fake-tool domain and a fresh .exe/.msi/.dll/.zip dropped into Downloads/Temp by that same browser process. Catches the click-handoff step where the CloudFront JS staging layer converts a 'Download' click into a TDS-gated payload. Rationale: The article describes the 'Download' button click as a click-interception handoff via CloudFront JS to a TDS. A 5-minute browser→file-drop window keyed off contact with one of the 8 named domains converts the noisy 'browser dropped a file' signal into a high-fidelity TDS-delivery signal. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/ • https://www.fullstory.com/blog/
ATT&CKT1189 T1204.002

[LLM] SessionGate final-stage rundll32 spawning cmd.exe to fetch and silently execute next-stage payload Installation High
Detects the SessionGate end-of-chain behaviour described in the article: a DLL loaded via rundll32.exe spawning cmd.exe to download and silently execute the unique-per-client next-stage malware. Specifically targets rundll32 living under user-writable paths (\AppData\, \Users\Public\) with cmd.exe carrying URL / download-utility tokens. Rationale: The article explicitly states the final DLL '...downloading and silently executing the next-stage malware via cmd.exe.' Pinning the detection on rundll32→cmd.exe with download-utility tokens or a user-writable parent path is article-specific and not covered by generic rundll32 abuse rules. The legitimate-pattern allowlist (printui, Control_RunDLL, mshtml PrintHTML) is the standard suppressor. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/
ATT&CKT1218.011 T1059.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "rundll32.exe"
| where FileName =~ "cmd.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","curl ","certutil","bitsadmin","powershell","Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\")
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("printui.dll","shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL","mshtml.dll,PrintHTML"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\rundll32.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\cmd.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","curl ","certutil","bitsadmin","powershell","Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ")
   or ParentProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("printui.dll","Control_RunDLL"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SessionGate rundll32 Spawning cmd.exe With Download Utility From User-Writable Path
id: 8b4f3c2d-7e2a-4d1b-a3c2-1f4d6e7a8b9c
description: Detects the SessionGate end-stage chain where a DLL loaded via rundll32 from AppData/Users\Public spawns cmd.exe to fetch and silently execute the next-stage payload.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fake-sites-mimicking-open-source-tools.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1218.011
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith: '\cmd.exe'
  selection_context:
    - CommandLine|contains:
        - 'http://'
        - 'https://'
        - 'curl '
        - 'certutil'
        - 'bitsadmin'
        - 'powershell'
        - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
    - ParentCommandLine|contains:
        - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
        - '\AppData\Roaming\'
        - '\Users\Public\'
  filter_legit:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'printui.dll'
      - 'shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL'
      - 'mshtml.dll,PrintHTML'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_context and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RUNDLL32.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE) AND (@CommandLine:(*http\:\/\/* OR *https\:\/\/* OR *curl* OR *certutil* OR *bitsadmin* OR *powershell* OR *Invoke-WebRequest*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\* OR *\\Users\\Public\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/rundll32\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\cmd\.exe$/i
| (regex("(?i)(http://|https://|curl |certutil|bitsadmin|powershell|Invoke-WebRequest|iwr )", field=CommandLine) OR regex("(?i)\\\\(AppData\\\\(Local|Roaming)|Users\\\\Public)\\\\", field=ParentCommandLine))
| NOT regex("(?i)(printui\.dll|shell32\.dll,Control_RunDLL|mshtml\.dll,PrintHTML)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=t count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes WHERE Processes.parent_process_name="rundll32.exe" Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" (Processes.process IN ("*http://*","*https://*","*curl *","*certutil*","*bitsadmin*","*powershell*","*Invoke-WebRequest*","*iwr *") OR Processes.parent_process IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\Users\\Public\\*")) BY Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.process, Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes WHERE Processes.parent_process_name="rundll32.exe" Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" (Processes.process IN ("*http://*","*https://*","*curl *","*certutil*","*bitsadmin*","*powershell*","*Invoke-WebRequest*","*iwr *") OR Processes.parent_process IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\Users\\Public\\*")) BY Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.process, Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Remus/Lumma Stealer browser-credential and crypto-wallet directory enumeration Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for a single non-browser process touching three or more files across Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Brave Login Data stores AND/OR Exodus/Electrum/Atomic/Ledger Live/Coinomi/Bitcoin/Zcash wallet directories. Targets the Remus Stealer behaviour (article: 'steal data from more than 20 browsers...cryptocurrency wallets, two-factor authentication tools, and password managers'). Rationale: Article explicitly lists Remus Stealer's targets: 'more than 20 browsers, hundreds of browser extensions and applications, cryptocurrency wallets, two-factor authentication tools, and password managers'. The composite test — same non-browser process touching ≥3 distinct credential/wallet artefacts in a short window — is the canonical stealer fan-out signature and is robust to whichever variant of Remus/Lumma is delivered. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1167/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let WindowDays = 7d;
let WalletPaths = dynamic([@"\AppData\Roaming\Exodus\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Electrum\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Atomic\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Ledger Live\",@"\AppData\Local\Coinomi\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Zcash\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Bitcoin\"]);
let CredPaths = dynamic([@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Login Data",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles",@"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\Default\Login Data"]);
let LegitProcs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","explorer.exe","SearchIndexer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","svchost.exe","Bitwarden.exe","1Password.exe"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(WindowDays)
| where FolderPath has_any (WalletPaths) or FolderPath has_any (CredPaths)
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (LegitProcs))
| summarize FilesTouched=dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),
            SamplePaths=make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 10),
            FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where FilesTouched >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
let WindowDays = 7d;
let WalletPaths = dynamic([@"\AppData\Roaming\Exodus\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Electrum\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Atomic\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Ledger Live\",@"\AppData\Local\Coinomi\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Zcash\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Bitcoin\"]);
let CredPaths = dynamic([@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Login Data",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles",@"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\Default\Login Data"]);
let LegitProcs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","explorer.exe","SearchIndexer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","svchost.exe","Bitwarden.exe","1Password.exe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (WalletPaths) or TargetFilePath has_any (CredPaths)
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ (LegitProcs))
| summarize FilesTouched=dcount(TargetFilePath),
            SamplePaths=make_set(TargetFilePath, 10),
            FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where FilesTouched >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:(11 OR 23) @TargetFilename:(*\\AppData\\Roaming\\Exodus\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Electrum\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Atomic\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Ledger?Live\\* OR *\\AppData\\Local\\Coinomi\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Zcash\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Bitcoin\\* OR *\\Chrome\\User?Data\\Default\\Login?Data* OR *\\Edge\\User?Data\\Default\\Login?Data* OR *\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\Profiles* OR *\\Brave-Browser\\User?Data\\Default\\Login?Data*) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\explorer.exe OR *\\SearchIndexer.exe OR *\\MsMpEng.exe)
#event_simpleName=/^(FileWritten|FileOpenInfo)$/ TargetFileName=/\\(AppData\\(Roaming|Local)\\(Exodus|Electrum|Atomic|Ledger Live|Coinomi|Zcash|Bitcoin)|Chrome\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data|Edge\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data|Mozilla\\Firefox\\Profiles|Brave-Browser\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|explorer|SearchIndexer|MsMpEng|svchost)\.exe$/i

[LLM] AnimateClipper ClickFix paste-to-run via explorer.exe spawning mshta/powershell/cmd Exploitation High
Detects the ClickFix delivery pattern used by AnimateClipper where the lure tricks the user into pasting a malicious command into the Windows Run dialog, producing an explorer.exe → mshta.exe/powershell.exe/cmd.exe chain carrying URL or base64 tokens. Pinned to the clipboard-paste characteristics described in the article. Rationale: Article calls out AnimateClipper as 'delivered by means of a ClickFix lure'. ClickFix's canonical artefact is explorer.exe (the Run-dialog host) as parent of an interpreter or LOLBin with a URL or base64-encoded payload on the cmd line — a tight signature that is article-specific, not the generic encoded-PowerShell rule. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/004/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001 T1218.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","FromBase64String","DownloadString","DownloadFile","IEX","Invoke-Expression","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","javascript:","mshtml:","Set-Clipboard","hidden")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\mshta.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","FromBase64String","DownloadString","DownloadFile","IEX","Invoke-Expression","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","javascript:","mshtml:","Set-Clipboard","hidden")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ClickFix Paste-to-Run via Explorer Spawning Script/LOLBin
id: 5c2d8f1e-3a4b-4c5d-9e1a-2b3c4d5e6f7a
description: Detects the ClickFix lure technique used by AnimateClipper and other campaigns where a user is tricked into pasting a malicious one-liner into the Windows Run dialog, yielding an explorer.exe parent for mshta/powershell/cmd carrying a URL or base64 payload.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fake-sites-mimicking-open-source-tools.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1204.004
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1218.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'IEX'
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc '
      - 'javascript:'
      - 'mshtml:'
      - 'Set-Clipboard'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\EXPLORER.EXE) @Image:(*\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe) @CommandLine:(*http\:\/\/* OR *https\:\/\/* OR *FromBase64String* OR *DownloadString* OR *DownloadFile* OR *IEX* OR *Invoke-Expression* OR *-EncodedCommand* OR *javascript\:* OR *mshtml\:* OR *Set-Clipboard*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/explorer\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\(mshta|powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(https?://|FromBase64String|DownloadString|DownloadFile|IEX|Invoke-Expression|-EncodedCommand|-enc |javascript:|mshtml:|Set-Clipboard)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

     | rename Processes.user as user]

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1204.002

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_parent:

            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'

            - 'wget '

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

High

Hackers Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months

The Hacker News
2026-06-04 14 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Unknown attackers spent at least five months inside the Outlook mailbox of a senior executive at a major global stock exchange, copying the inbox out in small, repeated batches and routing it through Dropbox and OneDrive so the traffic blended into normal cloud activity. Symantec and Carbon Black's Threat Hunter Team reported the campaign this week. This points to espionage, not a money grab:

ATT&CKT1053.005 T1190 T1195.002 T1528 T1555.003 T1566
